title: Make the negative end-to-end reconciliation test truly disagree
summary: Retry of 160432-g1tq. Fix the negative test a_result_whose_totals_disagree_with_model_usage_is_flagged_end_to_end so it builds the record, through the same parse and record path as the positive test, from an event whose totals really disagree. It then asserts check_invocation returns a Reconciliation violation. The audience is the Athena owner, who needs verified jobs to land.

defaults_applied.how: cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
The criteria check that the disagreement is detected through the real parse and record path, not that a test exists.
The test input must violate the invariant it claims to violate.
Only the test, plus the changelog if needed.
The verifier runs cargo test to exercise the behavior.
Fixture comments explain why each event is built the way it is.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The repository snapshot already holds the modelUsage definition (stream.rs, claude.rs output_from_result), a legacy-free check_invocation, and both end-to-end tests in crates/athena-core/src/invocation.rs. The remaining work is checking and tightening them, not re-implementing.

Under the single modelUsage definition, the measured tokens come from the requested model's modelUsage entry. A through-path disagreement is therefore reachable only in the costs (total_cost_usd against the modelUsage costUSD sum), unless the parser falls back to top-level usage. The test and changelog say so.

The negative test names the exact disagreement it builds and asserts that the input is bad before calling check_invocation. It also asserts that the violation is the sum comparison, not the 'no usage for the requested model' branch.
Any hand-edited-record case is labelled a gate-only check and is not presented as the through-path case.

The producer shows the negative test fails when the cost comparison in check_invocation is disabled. It reports this in its output, then restores the check, and the final diff leaves the check intact.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: a_result_whose_totals_disagree_with_model_usage_is_flagged_end_to_end passes. It builds the record from a result event with modelUsage for the requested model and a total_cost_usd that differs from the per-model costUSD sum. It uses the same parse and record-building helper as the positive test. It asserts, before calling check_invocation, that the record's reported total differs from the modelUsage sum. It then asserts exactly one Reconciliation violation whose detail names the per-model cost sum.

Run `cargo test`: the positive test a_result_whose_top_level_usage_includes_a_subagent_reconciles_end_to_end still passes. The job 2fsa top-level usage 90/52656/3634696/134508 differs from the modelUsage of 6/3136/275219/3821, the record carries the modelUsage tokens, and check_invocation returns no violations.

The negative test has no case that edits a built record by hand and calls it end-to-end. Any such case is labelled a gate-only check. The doc comments on the test and the fixtures state that token disagreement cannot arise through the parser under the modelUsage definition.
CHANGELOG.md records the fix and the modelUsage definition. It states honestly which disagreement the end-to-end negative test covers.
Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass and are clean, including the existing stream, claude, gate and landing tests.

out_of_scope: Changing the reconciliation rule or the modelUsage definition beyond what the tests need.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows.
A general mutation-testing framework for negative tests.
departures: The repository already holds most of the fix and both end-to-end tests, so this is a narrower change than the reference. I raised p_verification_passes slightly and lowered cost.
